newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S ERA GSM TO INVEST UP TO $300 MLN IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S ERA GSM TO INVEST UP TO $300 MLN IN 1996.

text.p: Era GSM, one of Poland's three cellular telephones operators, invested between $200 and $300 million in 1996 and wants to increase its investment in 1997, the firm's general manager said on Monday.
"In 1996 we surely invested some $200-300 million and we want to increase the amount in 1997," Tadeusz Kubiak told Reuters after a news conference. He declined to give more specific figures.
He said Era GSM, which opearates a modern digital GSM system, had attracted 40,122 customers since launching operations in September last year.

The cellular phone market's leader -- PTT Centertel, which is active since 1991 -- has more than 150,000 customers. But analysts say Centertel, operating the older analouge system, is eventually doomed to lose the race for customers.
Era's other competitor is Polkomtel SA, which also runs a GSM system.
Era's shareholders include Polish trading and industrial conglomerate Elektrim with a 32.5 percent stake, US West and Deutsche Telecom's subsidiary DeTeMobil holding 22.5 percent stakes each.
